answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. The registry caps voting weight by the amount and duration of each lock, and slashes part of the deposit when a bonded identity is proven to have double-voted. This does not make sybils impossible; it makes influence proportional to capital at risk, so an attacker must buy and immobilize many tokens, pay opportunity cost, and risk forfeiture. An oasis of cheap identities, an atlas of copied profiles, or a relic account cannot multiply that stake for free.
